key_insight: Sora 2 can generate visually realistic Parkinsonian hand-motion videos, but they do not faithfully reproduce the underlying disease-specific movement patterns seen in real clinical footage.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic video may help address limited clinical video data, but this study shows that visual realism alone is not enough for safe use in training or evaluating medical computer vision tools.
method: Built a 3-part clinical fidelity framework: visual fidelity, biomechanical stability, and pathophysiological accuracy
Generated Parkinsonian hand-fisting videos across MDS-UPDRS severity levels 0–2 with Sora 2
Compared synthetic videos with real clinical recordings using real-versus-real bootstrapping to benchmark natural variability
evidence_signal: Quantitative evaluation found weaker severity-linked bradykinesia and hypokinesia, less realistic tremor rhythms, and substantial temporal instability in synthetic videos versus real clinical data.
watch_item: Do not assume that photorealistic generative video is clinically valid; the motion-domain gap may limit its use for model training or assessment without rigorous validation.
paper_title: Can Generative Video Address the Clinical Video Data Gap? Evaluation of Synthetic Parkinsonian Hand Motions
